title: Unique Word Abbreviation
statement:
A word's *abbreviation* is its first letter, then the count of letters strictly between the first and the last letter (written in decimal), then its last letter: `"dog"` becomes `"d1g"` and `"internationalization"` becomes `"i18n"`. A word of one or two letters is its own abbreviation (`"it"` stays `"it"`).

Build a class `ValidWordAbbr`:

- `ValidWordAbbr(dictionary)` stores the list of words `dictionary`, which may contain repeats.
- `isUnique(word)` returns `true` when every dictionary word with the same abbreviation as `word` is exactly `word` itself (this includes the case where no dictionary word shares the abbreviation), and `false` when some dictionary word that differs from `word` has the same abbreviation.
constraints: dictionary[i] contains only lowercase English letters
word contains only lowercase English letters
At most 5000 calls are made to isUnique
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing a query with every dictionary word costs O(n) per call, and there can be thousands of calls. All a query needs to know about its abbreviation is: which distinct dictionary words have it? And only three answers matter: none, exactly one (and is it the query itself?), or two or more different words. So precompute, for each abbreviation, the single distinct word that owns it, or a marker that several different words share it.

## Approach

1. In the constructor, abbreviate each dictionary word with `abbreviate`.
2. If the abbreviation `abbr` is new, record the word as its owner in `owner`.
3. If it is already owned by a different word, set the owner to `null`: two different words clash. A repeat of the same word changes nothing.
4. `isUnique(word)`: if no dictionary word has `abbr`, return `true`.
5. Otherwise return whether the recorded owner is exactly `word`. A `null` owner never equals a word, so a clash gives `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

The dictionary `["deer","door","cake","card"]` abbreviates to `d2r`, `d2r`, `c2e`, `c2d`. `deer` and `door` differ, so `owner` holds `d2r -> null`, `c2e -> "cake"`, `c2d -> "card"`.
- `"dear"` is `d2r`, owned by `null`: `false`.
- `"cart"` is `c2t`, not in `owner`: `true`.
- `"cane"` is `c2e`, owned by `"cake"`: `false`.
- `"make"` is `m2e`, not in `owner`: `true`.
- `"cake"` is `c2e`, owned by `"cake"` itself: `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n * L) to build, where `L <= 20` is the word length, then O(L) per `isUnique` call.
- Space: O(n * L) for the map.

## Pitfalls

- A dictionary may repeat a word; `["a","a"]` must not count as a clash, so compare the words, not just the number of words per abbreviation.
- A query that is itself in the dictionary is still not unique if another, different word shares its abbreviation.
- Recording only whether an abbreviation appears is not enough: `isUnique("cake")` is `true` when `cake` is the sole owner, so keep the owner word too.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `owner` | maps an abbreviation to the one distinct dictionary word that has it, or `null` if several do |
| `abbr` | the abbreviation of the current word |
| `abbreviate(word)` | builds the abbreviation: first letter, middle count, last letter |
